findings.text: Loader supplies a file-operation table for 64-bit compressed kernel images, binding image recognition, loading with companion blobs, resource release, and optional signature confirmation when that build option is active.

Initialization entry creates a processor-specific top directory for debug views and, when boot-parameter introspection is compiled in, populates the nested boot-parameter subtree, returning any failure from that subordinate construction.

Recognition entry examines a candidate file header and accepts only images meeting size, signature, version and capability requirements for 64-bit high-loaded kernels compatible with current paging and firmware mode.

Load entry consumes kernel bytes plus optional initial filesystem and command text and produces loader-private state retaining the staged parameter block, after placing purgatory, parameters, kernel and filesystem into chosen physical ranges.
Release entry disposes the staged parameter allocation retained in loader-private state and clears the reference, tolerating absent state as success.
Loader-private record retains exactly one pointer to the temporary combined parameter area, whose lifetime spans successful load until cleanup; no other members appear in the routed material.

Debug view exposes processor boot information under a fixed nested hierarchy with top directory x86 containing boot_params holding version and data plus setup_data whose decimally named children each expose type and data through numeric and payload accessors.

Setup-data enumeration follows the physical chain head recorded in the live boot header, briefly mapping each descriptor to learn its successor, unwrapping at most one indirection layer, recording address, kind and length in heap nodes, and creating one child view per link until the chain terminates.

Initial filesystem placement is represented by splitting both address and length into low portions kept in the classic header and high portions kept in extension fields, preserving full wide values across the legacy layout.

Final command text lives inside the staged parameter area past the fixed header, is guaranteed terminated, carries elfcorehdr and optionally dmcryptkeys address options ahead of caller text for crash loads, and its physical location is likewise split between classic and extension pointer fields.
Memory map supplied to the next kernel is a prefix of the kexec-reserved map, truncated when necessary to the zero-page capacity, with its count recorded alongside the copied descriptors.

Optional payloads for random seed, firmware description, device tree, integrity measurement and handover are each encoded as typed length-delimited descriptors linked by prepending to the header chain head, so later additions become the new head without disturbing earlier links.

Firmware state is carried forward only when runtime services are active and a current memory map exists; the next parameter block inherits firmware identity and table references and receives a copied runtime map plus a descriptor for vendor and table addresses, while the platform configuration address falls back through newer to older firmware table pointers when initially absent.

Staged boot parameters inherit subarchitecture, display description, platform configuration address and disk description from live state, clear power-management and drive descriptors, derive legacy extended-memory indicators from the RAM extent covering the one-megabyte boundary with upper saturation, and preserve disk and signature buffers.

An image is accepted only when it spans at least two sectors, carries signature HdrS and the expected sector marker, meets a minimum protocol level, requests high loading and 64-bit loading above four gigabytes, is compatible with current firmware width and paging depth, and otherwise is rejected with a format error.

Load reserves a single combined area for parameters, command text and optional descriptors with low-address floor and modest alignment, honors kernel alignment and preferred address subject to a low floor, places the optional filesystem on page granularity above a higher floor, and sizes the combined area to include worst-case crash options and enabled optional descriptors.

Seed insertion is skipped when the random source is not yet ready; device-tree carryover requires both caller request and availability; handover descriptor requires both metadata pieces; measurement descriptor requires a nonzero log size; firmware map copy is skipped when its size is zero.
Diagnostic output from this loader carries a fixed textual prefix identifying the 64-bit image handler.

Image handling progresses from recognition to loading to release: successful recognition permits loading which on success yields retained private state; release always succeeds and invalidates that state; any load failure discards the staged area and reports an error pointer rather than partial state.

Parameter construction starts from copied header and memory map, then conditionally extends the descriptor chain with firmware, device-tree, measurement, handover and seed entries while advancing a running offset, so disabled or inapplicable options simply leave their reserved space unused without breaking later offsets.

Failure to allocate a node or to map a descriptor during debug-view construction abandons the whole setup-data subtree and propagates a memory-exhaustion indication; a failure building that subtree likewise removes the enclosing boot-parameter view.

Loading rejects truncated kernels, overlong command text including room for crash-specific suffixes, missing stack_end or entry64_regs symbols in purgatory, and buffer-placement failures, releasing the staged area before reporting the cause.
Minimum physical load addresses are 0x3000 for purgatory staging and for parameter staging, 0x100000 for kernel placement, and 0x1000000 for initial-filesystem placement.
Reserved suffix capacities are 30 characters for elfcorehdr and 31 for dmcryptkeys; the random seed payload length is 32 bytes.

Image recognition requires at least protocol level 0x020C, sector marker 0xAA55, high-load and 64-bit and above-4G capability flags, and five-level paging compatibility when active; loading uses combined-area alignment 16, kernel entry at base plus 0x200, and loader identity 0xD0.
